scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing in selling my former roommate's video games. Let me go through this step by step. First, the situation: We were on a lease together, and when the lease was ending, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff but left some things behind, including around 60 video games for the PS4. He also left a note saying he didn't want to bring those games with him. I tried to contact him for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or let me know what to do with it. But he never responded. So, I took most of his things to the dump, but I kept the games. I figured I could sell them because there's a local game store that buys used games. They gave me $600 for all of them. Then, last week, I saw him at a party. We were polite, but when he asked about the move-out process, I told him it went well. He asked what I did with his stuff, and when I told him I sold the games, he got mad. He called me an asshole and wants his money back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing I can be held accountable for, but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this. Hmm, so from a legal standpoint, I'm in the clear. But morally, is it right to sell someone's stuff when they didn't respond to my attempts to contact them? I mean, he left the games behind, and in our area, if you don't dispose of your things, the landlord can have them removed, which can cost you money from your deposit. So, I was trying to help him avoid that by selling the games instead of having the landlord throw them away, which would have cost him money. But on the other hand, I sold his games without his permission. Even though he didn't respond, maybe I should have made more effort to contact him or at least left the games somewhere safe instead of selling them. Maybe I could have stored them until he came back or something. I also think about the value of the games. $600 is a decent amount, but I don't know if that's what the games were worth. Maybe he could have gotten more if he sold them himself. Or maybe he didn't want to sell them at all; perhaps he just didn't want to bring them with him when he moved out, but he still wanted to keep them. Another angle is the relationship aspect. We were roommates, and now he's upset. Even though legally I'm fine, the fact that he's angry and calling me names makes me feel bad. Maybe I should have handled it differently to maintain a better relationship, even if it meant not selling the games. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could have sold the games but given him the money, or kept the games in case he wanted them back. But since he didn't respond, I assumed he didn't care, which might not be a fair assumption. In the end, I think I did what I thought was best at the time, but maybe I should have considered his feelings more or found another way to handle his belongings without selling them. It's possible that selling them without his consent was the wrong move, even if it was legally permissible.
